sources.citation: Frye, Henrike. 2025. [Simbali dictionary] Simbali - English/Tok Pisin, FLEx export, 20 pp.). Bundle 'Dictionary' (smg_0000, created 2023-10-01) in: The Simbali Baining of Papua New Guinea: A community-based documentation project. London: Endangered Languages Archive, collection 0694 (ELDP IPF0398). hdl:2196/yojsbm5e-o9z7-4yki-c9n3-ev3uz33e172r
sources.note: No phonology content: a bare alphabetical lexicon (c. 500 headwords with POS and English/Tok Pisin glosses, some example phrases), pages 1-3 blank/title 'Simbali', no introduction, no orthography or pronunciation notes. Practical orthography; the only diacritic letter is <ē> (228 tokens); no stress marks, no tone marks, no IPA field.

sources.citation: Frye, Henrike. 2022-2024. The Simbali Baining of Papua New Guinea: A community-based documentation project. ELAR deposit dk0694 (58 document files, 5 FLEx databases) -- and any phonology sketch / thesis chapters arising from it (Universität zu Köln).
sources.note: The only modern first-hand documentation of Simbali; document bundles or FLEx lexicon may contain a phonology sketch or stress-marked forms; a forthcoming description by Frye would be the primary source.

sources.citation: Frye, Henrike (depositor). 2023. : photographed transcription notebook (43 pp.) for bundle 'Basic words: Swadesh list 1' (smg_0062, elicitation recorded 2023-03-28, 7 WAV + 7 MP4 + 14 ELAN files, all Open). In: The Simbali Baining of Papua New Guinea, ELAR collection 0694. hdl:2196/c6f7768d-4081-46ed-88c3-2ff80d0951ae
sources.note: Image-only PDF (no text): handwritten Simbali forms with Tok Pisin glosses keyed to ELAN file names (e.g. 'Swadesh-OAV-OFN-OBK-230328-1ra.eaf: 1. ngua - mi.. 4. ngi - yu'); no stress or tone marking; wordlist data only. The accompanying open WAV/ELAN recordings (Swadesh lists 1-2, 'Pronouns and verbs', 'The numbers') are primary audio from which stress could be measured, but contain no statement.

sources.citation: Grummitt, John. 2015. The Wheel of Vitality: An Approach to Rapid Vitality Assessment in New Britain. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2014-010. Dallas: SIL International. 20 pp.
sources.note: Nothing; purely a sociolinguistic vitality assessment (EGIDS-based) of five New Britain communities incl. Simbali [smg], 450 speakers. This is the '2012 SIL report' cited by Wikipedia/Ethnologue. Only SIL resource listed for smg (sil.org language page, Internet Archive copy 2015).

sources.citation: Stebbins, Tonya N. 2011. Mali (Baining) grammar. Pacific Linguistics 623. Canberra: ANU. (sister language Mali, mali1284; context only)
sources.note: For MALI, not Simbali: sec. 3.5 p.33 'Stress in Mali is not contrastive.. Mali seems to have a basic pattern.. in which stress tends to be fixed on the penultimate syllable of the phonological word. However.. I found quite a few exceptions.' Mentions Simbali only as a neighbouring Baining language (350 speakers); no Simbali phonology.

sources.citation: Stebbins, Tonya N. 2009. The Papuan languages of the Eastern Bismarcks: migration, origins and connections. In Bethwyn Evans (ed.), Discovering history through language: papers in honour of Malcolm Ross (Pacific Linguistics 605), 223-243. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Overview/comparative chapter; only phonological content is intervocalic lenition as an areal Baining/Kuot feature (sec. 3.3). States p.227: 'To date, only Mali has been thoroughly documented.. Published data on Baining languages other than Mali remains scarce at this stage.' Simbali appears only in lists and in the note that the author did fieldwork in the Simbali community.
